Hi Gleice, this is Mark Collins from Brightleaf Vitamins in Chicago. Thank you for your email. We are very interested in the Brazilian market. Before our call, I want to tell you three things. First, we are a small brand with twelve products, and our best product is vitamin D for adults. Second, we want a partner who really knows pharmacies, not only a person who sells. Third, our investment for Brazil this year is small, about fifty thousand dollars. On our call, please tell me your plan. What will you do in the first six months? And how will you find new pharmacies? I think Brazil will be a big opportunity for us. Talk to you on Tuesday.

When you pitch your project to a foreign brand, remember three simple rules. Rule one: start with the opportunity. Tell them why your market will grow. For example, the pharmacy market in Brazil is one of the biggest in the world. Rule two: make clear promises. Say I will, not maybe I can. A brand wants a partner who is sure. Rule three: talk about money in a simple way. How much is the investment? When will they see revenue, and when will they see a profit? Two or three numbers are enough. And finally, always end with a next step. For example: I will send you the plan on Friday. A pitch with a next step is a pitch that continues.

First, Gleice thanks Mark for the call. Then she says she is going to open her company in March. After that, she promises she will visit fifty pharmacy chains. Next, she explains that the investment is small and the revenue will grow. Finally, she promises she will send the full plan on Friday.
